_what: Generic machine set-up limits. The engine's source commit, its build, its computer config, a front door's Caddy (`binary`, `binary_files`) and every download address are the computer row's. One SSH connection carries every command of an apply (`ssh_reuse_path`, the ssh ControlPath, %C its connection hash, short enough for a socket name; `ssh_reuse_seconds`, how long it stays open after the last command). `prebuilt_store` is where the computer running an apply keeps programs built elsewhere, each file named by the BLAKE3 of its bytes (a row's unit `source.prebuilt.blake3`); `~` is that computer's home.

slot_start._what: What a slot must find free before apply boots it beside the slot that runs (`margin_bytes` over the memory it needs, read from the computer's MemAvailable). The memory needed is the unit's `start_headroom_bytes` when its row names one, else the larger of the running slots' own MemoryCurrent (summed over the slots that run) and the start peak the last switch measured (the new slot's MemoryPeak once it passed its checks, kept on the computer in the unit's state folder as `start-peak-bytes`). A slot that does not fit is not started: apply is refused, nothing is stopped, and the slot that runs keeps serving (Nov 21 2026, 9:47 PM CST: a 1.32 GB new slot beside a 1.26 GB old one on a 4 GB computer was killed by the kernel's global out-of-memory killer, and every site on the box timed out).

machine._what: What set-up-the-machine.sh installs: the apt packages and the ports the firewall admits (firewall_allow). A computer row's own `machine` object replaces any of these fields for that computer, and carries what only that computer needs: `node` ({ version, files: { <uname -m>: { url, sha256 } } }, the node release each unit `node_bin` folder gets when it has none; a computer with no unit that names a node_bin gets none), `downloads` (a toolchain a unit's source build needs is one), `files`, `apt_sources`. A computer whose firewall another program keeps names firewall_allow null.

unit_defaults._what: What a unit's template reads when its row gives none: the build link in its builds folder it runs (`current`; a slot runs `current-<slot>`), and the seconds systemd waits for its stop before it ends the unit (`stop_seconds`; a unit that finishes long calls on a stop names more, longer than its own drain), and when systemd keeps its folder under /run (`runtime_preserve`: `restart` keeps it only across a restart; units that share one folder, such as two slots of one program, say `yes`, so the slot that stops never removes the folder the other one serves from).

build_limits._what: What a source build on the computer may use, by the kind of build (its argv's program name; `default` for any other): `memory_max`, the memory at which the kernel ends the build alone, and `seconds`, how long it may run before it is ended and the apply fails with build_over_time. The build runs in a systemd scope with MemoryMax and MemorySwapMax=0 and no MemoryHigh: a MemoryHigh below the max only slows a build that outgrows it, for ever (Nov 21 2026, 8:07-8:21 PM CST: a build held at 150M of a 200M cap crawled at 93% memory pressure, never ended, and held the apply), so a build past its memory is ended at once and a build past its time is ended whole (Nov 21 2026, 6:12:04-6:12:29 PM CST: a site's npm ci with no cap on the 3.8 GB always-on, which has no swap, stalled every site it served for 25 s). Sized for an 8 GB computer that also runs an engine (about 1.4 GB), a database and its sites. A unit's `source.limits` ({ memory_max, seconds }, either) replaces its kind's value.
